oewn-13837661-n.learner: The way two or more things, or parts of things, compare with each other in amount, size, or degree.
examples: His resentment was in proportion to the distress of his circumstances

oewn-13837954-n.learner: The number you get when you divide the size of a part by the size of the whole.
examples: If 3 of the 10 balls are red, the proportion of red balls is 0.3.

oewn-05098398-n.learner: How big something is, or how far it reaches.
examples: By spring the problem had grown to enormous proportions.

oewn-05083996-n.learner: A pleasing way in which the parts of something, such as a design, are arranged and fit together as a whole.
examples: The architect was praised for the fine proportion of the front of the house.

oewn-13921008-n.learner: A balance among the parts of something.
examples: The statue's head is too big and throws the whole figure out of proportion.
since this sad affair has taken place, it is said that he left Meryton greatly in debt
I am truly rejoiced that my cousin Lydia's sad business has been so well hushed up

connotation.why: calls a situation regrettably bad rather than just describing it

oewn-01364779-a.learner: Feeling or showing sorrow or unhappiness.
examples: She looked sad when her friend moved away.

oewn-01369193-s.learner: Making you feel sorrow or unhappiness.
examples: It was a sad story about a lost child.

oewn-02622766-v.learner: To keep yourself alive by getting what you need to live.
examples: Through the long winter the family subsisted on bread and potatoes.
A small sum could not do all this.
instead of spending his whole income, he had laid by an annual sum

oewn-05869651-n.learner: The number you get when you add a group of numbers together.
examples: The sum of 4 and 5 is 9.
A good team is more than the sum of its players.

oewn-07975630-n.learner: The final total that everything adds up to.
examples: The sum of all their small mistakes was one great failure.

oewn-05929717-n.learner: The best, most basic, or most important part of an idea or experience.
examples: The sum of his long speech was that we should wait.

oewn-08015154-n.learner: A set that holds all the members of two or more given sets, and nothing else.
examples: The sum of the sets {1, 2} and {2, 3} is {1, 2, 3}.

oewn-13992548-n.learner: A calm state in which nothing troubles or disturbs you.
examples: But not long was the interval of tranquillity

oewn-07530799-n.learner: A state of peace and quiet.
examples: They moved to the countryside for its tranquillity.

oewn-01069743-n.learner: The act of putting things off on purpose and playing when you should be working.
examples: The teacher had no patience for trifling during lessons.

connotation.why: frames play as time wasted when work is due

oewn-02718424-n.learner: A large room or area at the entrance of a building, where people come in or are received.
examples: She was met in the vestibule by Lydia
Lydia's voice was heard in the vestibule; the door was thrown open, and she ran into the room.

oewn-05312102-n.learner: Any of several hollow spaces in the body that lead into another space, such as in the ear or the vagina.
examples: The vestibule of the inner ear helps the body keep its balance.
She is abominably rude to keep Charlotte out of doors in all this wind.
it will be abominably rude if you do not wait on him.

connotation.why: strong disapproval where 'badly' or 'very' would be plain

oewn-00311025-r.learner: In a way that is offensive and full of hate.
examples: After abusing you so abominably to your face, I could have no scruple in abusing you to all your relations.

connotation.why: brands the behaviour as hateful, not just bad

oewn-04642461-n.learner: The quality of being active, moving or acting quickly and with energy.
examples: They were soon gone again, rising from their seats with an activity which took their brother by surprise

oewn-00408356-n.learner: Any particular thing that someone does.
examples: Swimming is her favourite weekend activity.
After his long illness he slowly returned to activity.

oewn-13540166-n.learner: A process that happens in nature, not one that people cause on purpose.
examples: Scientists watched the mountain for signs of volcanic activity.

oewn-13461236-n.learner: A natural process that takes place inside the body.
examples: The scan showed normal brain activity.

oewn-14554805-n.learner: In chemistry, how able a substance is to take part in a chemical reaction.
examples: Heat can raise the activity of the catalyst.

oewn-04639057-n.learner: The quality of being active, full of spirit, or alive and full of energy.
examples: The evening conversation, when they were all assembled, had lost much of its animation

oewn-00553473-n.learner: Movement and activity going on in general.
examples: As the fair opened, the streets filled with noise and animation.

oewn-00910103-n.learner: The work of making cartoons in which drawings seem to move.
examples: She studied animation and now makes cartoons for television.

oewn-01050390-n.learner: The act of giving life and energy to something.
examples: The animation of the dull party was left to her.
The doctor looked for any sign of animation in the still body.

oewn-05012993-n.learner: The power to stay alive and grow.
examples: Some seeds keep their animation for years in a dry place.
